# Incident Report: MTA-2021-09-10 Traffic Analysis Exercise

## 1. Victim Host

| Attribute | Value |
|---|---|
| IPv4 address | **10.9.10.102** |
| MAC address | **00:4f:49:b1:e8:c3** |
| Windows hostname | **DESKTOP-KKITB6Q** (NetBIOS group/domain: `ANGRYPOUTINE`, AD domain `angrypoutine.com`) |
| Logged-in user | **hobart.gunnarsson** (confirmed via Kerberos AS-REQ/TGS-REQ CNameString from 10.9.10.102 to the domain controller 10.9.10.9) |

Grounding: DHCP transaction shows the host requesting/leasing an address with `Host Name: DESKTOP-KKITB6Q` and MAC `00:4f:49:b1:e8:c3`; NBNS registrations from 10.9.10.102 confirm the same hostname and workgroup name; Kerberos traffic to the domain controller (10.9.10.9, `angrypoutine-dc.angrypoutine.com`) shows the client principal `hobart.gunnarsson`.

## 2. Malware Family

**IcedID (aka BokBot)** — attribution is **behavioral/pattern-based**, not signature-confirmed (no IDS/AV alert export was present in the evidence directory to cite as a hard signature match). The behavioral basis:

- A fake-update/gate-style HTTP GET with a spoofed old user-agent (`Mozilla/4.0 (compatible; MSIE 7.0; Windows NT 10.0...)`) to a random multi-segment URL path, delivering a Windows PE32+ **DLL** payload disguised as a generic web response (`Content-Type: application/octet-stream`) — a well-known IcedID first-stage loader delivery pattern.
- Post-infection, the host immediately begins periodic HTTPS "check-in" connections to two different IPs that present the **identical self-signed TLS certificate** (`CN=londonareloeli.uk, O=LL EST, OU=UK System, L=London, ST=London, C=GB`) with **no SNI extension** sent — a distinctive, non-CDN, direct-IP-to-cert-reuse pattern consistent with IcedID's C2 beaconing infrastructure, repeating roughly every few minutes for the remainder of the capture (~76 minutes).

## 3. Indicators of Compromise

**Malicious domain**
- `simpsonsavingss.com` → resolved to `194.62.42.206`

**Malicious URL (initial payload delivery / gate)**
- `http://simpsonsavingss.com/bmdff/BhoHsCtZ/MLdmpfjaX/5uFG3Dz7yt/date1?BNLv65=pAAS`
  - GET request at t=140.04s from 10.9.10.102 to 194.62.42.206:80, User-Agent spoofed as old IE7 on Windows NT 10.0
  - HTTP 200 response at t=142.18s, `Content-Type: application/octet-stream`, 284,816 bytes

**Transferred file**
- Payload file (as served, path segment `date1?BNLv65=pAAS`)
- File type: **PE32+ executable (DLL), x86-64, GUI subsystem**
- **SHA256: `eed363fc4af7a9070d69340592dcab7c78db4f90710357de29e3b624aa957cf8`**

**Command-and-control endpoints (post-infection HTTPS beacons)**
- `167.172.37.9:443` — single TLS session ~2 seconds after the DLL download completed (t≈144.06s)
- `94.158.245.52:443` — repeated/periodic TLS sessions from t≈148.7s through the end of the capture (t≈4512s), roughly every 2–10 minutes
- Both C2 endpoints presented the same self-signed certificate: `CN=londonareloeli.uk` (O=LL EST, OU=UK System, L/ST=London, C=GB), and neither TLS ClientHello carried an SNI value — both are anomalous relative to all other TLS traffic on this host, which was otherwise legitimate Microsoft/Windows telemetry and update traffic (msedge.net, windowsupdate.com, live.com, officeapps.live.com, etc.)

## 4. Summary Timeline

| Time (rel.) | Event |
|---|---|
| t=140.0s | GET to `simpsonsavingss.com` (194.62.42.206), spoofed IE7 UA |
| t=142.2s | HTTP 200, 284,816-byte DLL payload delivered |
| t=144.1s | First C2 TLS connection to 167.172.37.9:443 (self-signed `londonareloeli.uk` cert, no SNI) |
| t=148.7s onward | Recurring C2 TLS beacons to 94.158.245.52:443 (same cert), continuing to end of capture |

All other traffic from 10.9.10.102 (Windows Update/Delivery Optimization CAB/EXE downloads, Microsoft Edge/Office telemetry, LDAP/Kerberos/SMB domain traffic, NBNS/mDNS/SSDP broadcast noise) is consistent with normal enterprise workstation activity and shows no additional signs of compromise.
